results.title: A Year of Energy Storage Supply Chain Tariffs, Tech and ...
results.content: Tariffs dominate the supply chain conversation. Recent trade actions have increased the cost of critical, imported materials and components, including those linked to lithium battery production. These increases are not limited to direct imports − they move through domestic suppliers who rely on foreign-sourced raw materials. This is pushing manufacturers to re-evaluate procurement strategies. [...] The cost barrier for onshoring and nearshoring remains a significant issue for the hundreds of small- or mid-sized battery providers in the U.S. To better afford domestic manufacturing investments, many companies may begin consolidating through partnerships, joint ventures, or mergers and acquisitions − a trend that stands to strengthen the entire supply chain over the long term. [...] Additionally, the Critical Mineral Transparency and Reporting in Advanced Clean Energy (TRACE) Act, known to many as H.R. 8187, is a proposed U.S. bill that aims to increase accountability in the sourcing and use of critical minerals. If enacted, the legislation would require digital tracking identifiers for battery components and minerals throughout their lifecycle. This move signals a shift toward deep supply chain traceability as a baseline for market participation.

results.title: Global Impact of Tariffs on Supply Chains
results.content:
The impact of tariffs on supply chain costs is immediate and widespread. When tariffs rise, prices for steel, aluminum, resins, and plastics increase. These materials are essential for packaging production, so even small changes affect overall expenses. As costs grow, shipping and freight rates often climb as well. Supplier contracts may also need renegotiation to reflect higher import fees and compliance requirements. [...] Tariffs have always been part of global trade, but the last several years have introduced new layers of complexity for executives managing supply chains. The impact of tariffs on supply chains goes far beyond customs paperwork. It reshapes costs, squeezes budgets, and places enormous pressure on leaders trying to balance operational efficiency with financial constraints. [...] ### Consumer Electronics Complexity

Tariffs are increasing costs for key electronic components and protective packaging. Plastics, foams, and aluminum materials face higher import duties, straining supply chains. Manufacturers are having to adjust sourcing strategies to meet launch schedules and protect fragile products. These cost pressures make maintaining consistent quality and margins more challenging worldwide.

[...] Storage batteries have been indicated as a priority for border detentions for forced labor evaluation, and we expect to continue seeing those goods identified as a concern. It will be key for companies to understand their supply chain for materials and finished goods and be prepared to respond quickly should US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) issue a questionnaire regarding the use of forced labor in the production of imported merchandise. [...] There is also a Section 232 investigation into critical minerals. In January 2026, the president issued a proclamation finding that processed critical minerals and their derivative products—including those essential for battery production, such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, manganese, and graphite—threaten US national security. The administration did not impose immediate tariffs, and instead initiated negotiations to address dependency on foreign supply chains (primarily focused on China).

results.title: Tariff Resources and Strategies | GaMEP at Georgia Tech
results.content:
## GaMEP Expertise

 Supply chain assessment: We evaluate your supply chain — from raw material to finished product — to identify risks and opportunities.
 Supplier scouting: We search for and connect you with qualified domestic suppliers.

 Process improvement: We apply lean practices to improve production and reduce costs.
 Technology automation: We analyze and help implement appropriate technologies. [...] Reshoring: Consider automation opportunities and domestic suppliers (including those who can expand their production).
 Nearshoring: Take advantage of duty-free imports through Mexico.
 Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States Chapter 98 and Chapter 99: Eliminate or reduce duties for qualifying products.
 Bonded warehouses: Store imported products while deferring duties until they leave the facility (quarterly harbor maintenance fees apply). [...] Foreign trade zones: Manufacture domestically while deferring or reducing duties based on the final product classification.
 First sale rule: Pay duties based on the manufacturer or middleman price (rather than the importer price).

## Tariff Resources

 Harmonized Tariff Schedule: View exempt products (updated regularly).
 U.S. Customs and Border Protection Centers of Excellence and Expertise (industry-specific):
  + Ask questions, such as how tariffs apply to specific industries.
